args: Native mobile accessibility as a design decision, plus the current legal enforcement landscape for digital accessibility. Narrow scope — two related halves. HALF ONE, native platform accessibility that a DESIGNER must decide, not a developer: (1) Apple Dynamic Type — the text style ramp, what sizes the accessibility sizes reach, what a designer must commit to for a layout to survive the largest accessibility text sizes, and Apple's stated guidance on layouts that must reflow or switch to vertical at large sizes; (2) VoiceOver on iOS — accessibility traits, labels vs hints vs values, the rotor and heading structure, what a designer decides about reading order and grouping; (3) Android TalkBack and the Android accessibility model — content descriptions, touch exploration, the recommended 48dp target and its relationship to WCAG, and Android's font scaling including non-linear font scaling introduced in Android 14; (4) what accessibility requirements differ between native and web such that a web-derived checklist misses them entirely. HALF TWO, legal drivers and their CURRENT enforcement state as of 2026: (5) the European Accessibility Act (Directive EU 2019/882) — what became applicable in June 2025, exactly which products and services are in scope, the microenterprise exemption and its thresholds, and what standard conformance is measured against (EN 301 549 and its relationship to WCAG); (6) the US DOJ ADA Title II web rule (28 CFR part 35 subpart H) — the technical standard it names, and its compliance deadlines by public entity size; (7) Section 508 and what standard it currently references; (8) whether any binding instrument yet names WCAG 2.2 rather than 2.1 or 2.0. Prioritize primary sources only: developer.apple.com Human Interface Guidelines accessibility pages, developer.android.com accessibility docs, EUR-Lex official directive text, ada.gov and the Federal Register, and the ETSI EN 301 549 standard text. Reject law-firm marketing blogs and accessibility-vendor content marketing where a primary source exists.
